verdict.rationale: Brex has a broad API surface: transactions, statements and accounts (read), budgets and spend limits, expenses with receipt upload, vendor creation and payments, users with rich filters, webhooks, onboarding referrals, and card issuance shown in integration examples. An MCP server also exposes expenses, users, cards, banking and bills to AI assistants. However, nothing documents parity with the UI, and many UI features (travel booking, multi-level approval-flow configuration, the AI audit/review agents, accounting setup) have no API evidence, while transactions appear to be read-only. Missing for 10: any explicit API/UI parity claim or coverage map, API evidence for travel booking, approval-policy configuration, AI agent controls and accounting integration, a publicly fetchable OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration of coverage.
